concept.name: PostgreSQL MVCC, 32-Bit XID Wraparound & Autovacuum Freezing
concept.title: PostgreSQL MVCC, 32-Bit XID Wraparound & Autovacuum Freezing

spark.summary: PostgreSQL's 32-bit transaction IDs (XIDs) wrap modulo 2^32 (~4.29B), splitting the ring into 2B past and 2B future; unless autovacuum freezes old tuples via HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN before age(relfrozenxid) nears 2B, the database halts all writes to prevent silent data loss.
spark.keyTakeaway: Long-running or idle-in-transaction snapshots pin the global xmin horizon, starving autovacuum of dead-tuple reclamation and advancing XID age toward the 2B emergency write-freeze wall.
spark.byteSummary:
PostgreSQL implements Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) by stamping every heap tuple header with 32-bit xmin and xmax transaction IDs instead of overwriting rows in place. Because 32-bit XIDs wrap around after 4.29 billion transactions, PostgreSQL compares them using modulo-2^32 circular arithmetic: ~2 billion XIDs behind the current XID are visible past, while ~2 billion ahead are invisible future.

To prevent old committed rows from suddenly appearing to be in the future after wraparound, autovacuum freeze workers scan pg_class.relfrozenxid and mark aged tuples with the HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN bit in t_infomask. Once a page's tuples are all frozen, the Visibility Map (VM) marks the page all-frozen so future anti-wraparound scans can skip it entirely.

Under high write rates (e.g., 30,000 updates/sec), an idle reporting transaction (`BEGIN; SELECT ...`), orphaned replication slot, or low default `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=200` pins the backend xmin horizon and blocks dead-tuple cleanup. Table bloat explodes 5x and XID age climbs toward the 2B emergency shutdown wall (~1M-3M XIDs remaining), forcing PostgreSQL into read-only mode until manual single-user VACUUM FREEZE completes.

learningJourney.title: Stage 1: MVCC Tuple Versioning (xmin, xmax & t_infomask)
learningJourney.purpose: Understand how PostgreSQL stores row versions in heap pages using xmin, xmax, and hint bits without in-place overwrites.
learningJourney.explanation: Every INSERT writes a new tuple with xmin set to the creating XID, and every UPDATE writes a brand-new tuple version while stamping the old version's xmax with the updating XID. Readers check tuple visibility against their snapshot's xmin/xmax bounds and t_infomask hint bits rather than acquiring read locks.

learningJourney.title: Stage 2: The 32-Bit Circular XID Ring & 2B Horizon
learningJourney.purpose: Explain modulo-2^32 XID arithmetic and why an unfrozen tuple older than 2B XIDs appears to be in the future.
learningJourney.explanation: PostgreSQL uses unsigned 32-bit integers (0 to 4,294,967,295) for normal XIDs. Circular comparison treats any XID within 2^31 (~2.14B) behind current_xid as past and any XID within 2^31 ahead as future. If a table's oldest unfrozen XID crosses 2B transactions behind current_xid, it wraps into the 'future' half of the ring and becomes invisible—causing silent data loss unless prevented.
learningJourney.codeExample:
MASK_32 = 0xFFFFFFFF
HALF_RING = 1 << 31

def xid_precedes(xid_a: int, xid_b: int) -> bool:
    diff = (xid_a - xid_b) & MASK_32
    return diff > HALF_RING

cards.label: High-Write Burn Rate
cards.detail: At 30,000 write XIDs/sec, a database consumes 2 billion XIDs in under 19 hours.

cards.label: Hard Safety Stop
cards.detail: PostgreSQL refuses new XIDs ~1M-3M before wraparound to guarantee zero silent data disappearance.

sectionDiagram.summary: Modulo-2^32 XID comparison divides 4.29B IDs into 2B past and 2B future, triggering a write halt before unfrozen rows wrap.
sectionDiagram.caption: 32-bit XID ring splits into 2B visible past and 2B invisible future, with a hard shutdown wall before wraparound.

learningJourney.title: Stage 3: HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN, relfrozenxid & the Visibility Map
learningJourney.purpose: Trace how autovacuum freeze workers mark aged tuples permanently visible and skip frozen pages via the Visibility Map.
learningJourney.explanation: When a tuple's age exceeds vacuum_freeze_min_age (default 50M), VACUUM sets bit 0x0200 (HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN) in t_infomask so all snapshots treat it as unconditionally older than any current XID. Once every tuple on an 8 KB heap page is frozen, the Visibility Map (VM) sets the page's all-frozen bit, allowing future anti-wraparound scans to skip the page and advance pg_class.relfrozenxid.

sectionDiagram.title: Advancing pg_class.relfrozenxid Without Full-Table Re-Scans

cards.label: Anti-Wraparound Priority
cards.detail: Anti-wraparound autovacuum runs even if autovacuum=off and cannot be permanently blocked by user locks.

cards.label: Visibility Map Payoff
cards.detail: Append-only/cold pages marked all-frozen are skipped on subsequent freeze sweeps, cutting I/O by 90%+.

sectionDiagram.summary: Autovacuum freeze workers set HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN on aged tuples and use the Visibility Map to skip already-frozen pages.
sectionDiagram.caption: Autovacuum checks relfrozenxid, skips all-frozen VM pages, sets HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN, and advances pg_class.relfrozenxid.

learningJourney.title: Stage 4: How Idle Transactions & Replication Slots Pin xmin
learningJourney.purpose: Diagnose how a single idle-in-transaction session or dead replication slot blocks tuple freezing across the entire cluster.
learningJourney.explanation: PostgreSQL computes a global oldest_xmin horizon across pg_stat_activity (active/idle-in-transaction sessions), prepared transactions (2PC), and pg_replication_slots (hot_standby_feedback). A single forgotten `BEGIN; SELECT ...` reporting session pins oldest_xmin at its start XID, preventing autovacuum from removing dead tuples or advancing xmin-dependent cleanup.

sectionDiagram.title: Three Silent Horizon Pinners That Starve Autovacuum

cards.label: 5x Table Bloat
cards.detail: While xmin is pinned, 30,000 updates/sec accumulate millions of unreclaimable dead tuples in heap pages.

cards.label: Diagnostic Query
cards.detail: Always inspect pg_stat_activity (state='idle in transaction') and pg_replication_slots (active=false).

sectionDiagram.summary: Idle-in-transaction sessions, inactive replication slots, and orphaned 2PC transactions pin global xmin and cause severe table bloat.
sectionDiagram.caption: Idle-in-transaction sessions, dead replication slots, and 2PC transactions pin global xmin and block vacuum reclamation.

learningJourney.title: Stage 5: Heap-Only Tuples (HOT) & fillfactor=70 Tuning
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate B-tree index write amplification and curb bloat on update-heavy ledgers using HOT updates.
learningJourney.explanation: Normally, every UPDATE must insert new index entries into every B-tree index on the table. If the updated columns are not indexed AND the same 8 KB heap page has free space, PostgreSQL performs a Heap-Only Tuple (HOT) update—chaining the new version on the same page with zero index writes. Setting `fillfactor=70` reserves 30% free space per page so 30K/s updates stay HOT.

sectionDiagram.title: Keeping 30,000 Updates/Sec Page-Local with fillfactor=70

cards.label: Zero Index Bloat
cards.detail: HOT updates avoid appending dead pointers to secondary B-tree indexes, slashing I/O and WAL volume.

cards.label: Page-Level Pruning
cards.detail: Subsequent readers opportunistically prune dead HOT chains inline without waiting for autovacuum.

sectionDiagram.summary: Reserving 30% page headroom via fillfactor=70 enables Heap-Only Tuple updates that avoid index writes and keep bloat under 5%.
sectionDiagram.caption: Non-indexed updates land on the same 8 KB page via fillfactor=70 headroom, avoiding B-tree writes and keeping bloat < 5%.

learningJourney.title: Stage 6: Autovacuum Cost-Limit Throttling & Multi-Worker Tuning
learningJourney.purpose: Remove the default autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=200 bottleneck so freeze workers keep pace with 30K updates/sec.
learningJourney.explanation: PostgreSQL's default `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=200` and `cost_delay=2ms` (or 20ms on older releases) throttle vacuum I/O to a crawl—allowing a 400 GB ledger at 30K updates/sec to generate dead tuples and XIDs faster than autovacuum can clean them. Raising `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000`, lowering `cost_delay=2ms`, and scaling `autovacuum_max_workers` lets freeze workers finish before XID age spikes.

sectionDiagram.title: Unthrottling Autovacuum from Default 200 to 2000 Cost Limit

cards.label: Per-Table Overrides
cards.detail: High-churn ledger tables can set aggressive storage parameters (cost_limit=2000) without starving batch analytics.

cards.label: NVMe Headroom
cards.detail: Modern NVMe SSDs sustain 100K+ IOPS, making default HDD-era vacuum throttling obsolete.

sectionDiagram.summary: Raising autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit to 2000 with 2ms delay and sufficient workers prevents vacuum starvation on high-churn tables.
sectionDiagram.caption: Scaling autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit from 200 to 2000 with parallel workers keeps relfrozenxid safely below 200M.

learningJourney.title: Stage 7: Emergency Recovery & Automated Prevention Guardrails
learningJourney.purpose: Establish automated timeouts, replication WAL caps, and XID-age alerting—plus safe single-user recovery if a freeze hits.
learningJourney.explanation: Preventing wraparound requires defense in depth: `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s` and `statement_timeout` kill zombie readers, `max_slot_keep_wal_size` bounds dead replication slots, and Prometheus alerts fire when `max(age(relfrozenxid)) > 150M`. If a cluster ever hits the 2B read-only wall, operators must terminate blockers, start PostgreSQL in `--single` mode, and run `VACUUM FREEZE`.

sectionDiagram.title: Defense-in-Depth Against XID Wraparound Outages

cards.label: 30-Second Zombie Kill
cards.detail: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s guarantees forgotten reporting transactions cannot pin xmin for hours.

cards.label: Early-Warning SLO
cards.detail: Alerting at 150M XIDs gives SREs hours of runway before the 200M anti-wraparound trigger or 2B shutdown.

sectionDiagram.summary: Enforcing 30s idle-in-transaction timeouts, bounded replication slots, and tiered XID-age alerts prevents wraparound write freezes.
sectionDiagram.caption: Session timeouts, max_slot_keep_wal_size, and tiered XID-age alerts protect clusters from hitting single-user recovery.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does PostgreSQL shut down all writes ~1M-3M XIDs before reaching the 2B transaction ID wraparound boundary?

options.text: To prevent unfrozen committed rows from wrapping into the 'future' half of the 32-bit XID ring and silently disappearing from queries.
options.feedback: Correct. In modulo-2^32 circular arithmetic, an XID > 2B behind current_xid looks like a future uncommitted transaction.

options.text: Because 32-bit integers overflow into negative floats in SQL.
options.feedback: Incorrect. XIDs are unsigned 32-bit integers compared modulo 2^32.

options.text: Because the Visibility Map deletes all heap pages at 2B XIDs.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The Visibility Map tracks all-visible and all-frozen pages; it never deletes heap data.

options.text: Because B-tree indexes only support 2 billion keys.
options.feedback: Incorrect. B-tree indexes are unrelated to the 32-bit XID wraparound limit.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: PostgreSQL halts writes before wraparound so no unfrozen committed tuple ever crosses the 2B midpoint and becomes invisible.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does a forgotten `BEGIN; SELECT ...` reporting session cause 5x table bloat on an update-heavy ledger?

options.text: It locks every table in ACCESS EXCLUSIVE mode.
options.feedback: Incorrect. A SELECT only takes ACCESS SHARE, which doesn't block writers directly.

options.text: It pins the global oldest_xmin horizon at its transaction start XID, preventing autovacuum from reclaiming any newer dead tuples.
options.feedback: Correct. Because the idle transaction might still read old row versions, VACUUM cannot remove dead tuples created after its xmin.

options.text: It disables HOT updates on all tables.
options.feedback: Incorrect. HOT updates depend on fillfactor and indexed columns, though dead HOT chains still wait on xmin for full reclamation.
Incorrect. It pins oldest_xmin, starving dead-tuple cleanup.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: An idle-in-transaction session holds an active snapshot, pinning global xmin and blocking autovacuum from reclaiming dead tuples.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does setting `fillfactor=70` dramatically reduce bloat and I/O on a 30,000 updates/sec PostgreSQL table?

options.text: It compresses each row by 30% using Zstandard.
options.feedback: Incorrect. fillfactor reserves free space on each 8 KB page; it does not compress rows.

options.text: It forces PostgreSQL to overwrite rows in place without MVCC.
options.feedback: Incorrect. PostgreSQL always writes new tuple versions for MVCC.

options.text: It reserves 30% free space per 8 KB heap page so non-indexed updates qualify as Heap-Only Tuples (HOT) with zero B-tree index writes.
options.feedback: Correct. HOT updates keep new versions on the same page and enable fast inline page pruning.

options.text: It increases XID width from 32-bit to 64-bit.
options.feedback: Incorrect. XIDs remain 32-bit in heap tuple headers.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: fillfactor=70 leaves 30% free space per page, enabling same-page HOT updates that eliminate secondary index write amplification.

beginner.summary: PostgreSQL keeps old row versions for active readers and cleans them up with autovacuum; if an idle transaction blocks cleanup, tables bloat and writes eventually freeze.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Setting a 30-second idle-in-transaction timeout and tuning autovacuum keeps tables small and prevents emergency write freezes.
beginner.byteSummary:
When you update a row in PostgreSQL, it writes a new copy and marks the old one dead until autovacuum cleans it up. If someone leaves a `BEGIN; SELECT` transaction open, autovacuum cannot remove those dead copies.

Setting short timeouts for idle transactions and giving autovacuum enough speed prevents table bloat and write shutdowns.

intermediate.summary: Prevent 5x bloat and XID wraparound freezes by pairing fillfactor=70 HOT updates, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s, and autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=2000.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: Eliminating xmin horizon pinners and unthrottling autovacuum I/O keeps bloat < 5% at 30,000 updates/sec.
intermediate.byteSummary:
On a 400 GB ledger taking 30,000 updates/sec, default `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit=200` and an idle reporting transaction pin `xmin`, causing 5x bloat and pushing `age(relfrozenxid)` toward 2B.

Combining `fillfactor=70` (HOT updates), a 30s idle-in-transaction timeout, and `cost_limit=2000` keeps bloat under 5%.

advanced.summary: Deep-dive into modulo-2^32 XID ring wraparound, HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN Visibility Map skipping, max_slot_keep_wal_size guards, and single-user VACUUM FREEZE recovery.
advanced.keyTakeaway: Defense in depth combines 30s session timeouts, bounded replication WAL, cost_limit=2000 multi-worker freezing, and tiered XID-age alerts (150M/500M/1.5B).
advanced.byteSummary:
PostgreSQL's 32-bit XID ring splits 4.29B IDs into 2B past and 2B future. Autovacuum sets `HEAP_XMIN_FROZEN` (`0x0200`) and marks Visibility Map pages all-frozen to advance `pg_class.relfrozenxid` without re-scanning cold pages.

Hardening high-churn clusters requires killing `backend_xmin` pinners (`idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s`), bounding dead slots (`max_slot_keep_wal_size`), unthrottling `cost_limit=2000`, and alerting at 150M XIDs long before single-user `VACUUM FREEZE` is needed.
